title: AUDIT CORRECTION: COMPLAINT-1 diluted arm (b), pseudo-replicated kinds, and used broken critique regex
question: Audit of COMPLAINT-1 design, timing, code, and conclusions
design: Audit against simharness/complaint1.py @ 988b0aa0a and GCS outputs gs://usersim-bakeoff-347838016394/usersim_sim/simharness/bench_v0/ceiling1/complaint1/
scoring_fixed_before_results: Audit check: code b4f0babda committed 21:22:39Z BEFORE ledger registration 2ac9604fa at 21:24:17Z; complaint1.json written 21:32:56Z
what_ran: Verified complaint1.json ($1.578, 2,164 calls, 22 launches x 8 resamples = 176 rows). Numbers in complaint1.json match results, EXCEPT major undocumented methodological defects invalidate the 'both arms closed' decision.
deviations: TIMING: simharness/complaint1.py was committed at 21:22:39Z (b4f0babda) before ledger registration at 21:24:17Z (2ac9604fa).

SEVERE DILUTION BUG (complaint1.py:204-209): b_critical = A['persona'] (~22 items) + A['critical_pb'] (15 items), then subsampled to half-A size (median 8.5) using identical RNG indices as deployed. ~60% of b_critical's scored items are literally identical strings to deployed; critical_pb was never tested standalone at equal size.

BROKEN CRITIQUE FILTER (complaint1.py:44-46): CRIT regex matches 'but', 'though', 'already', 'don't', 'wish', 'trust', classifying generic PH praise as critical (median critical pool = 441 people/launch).

PSEUDO-REPLICATION (complaint1.py:262-275): '787 half-B complaints' is not 787 distinct complaints; it sums 176 resample extractions across the same 22 launches (~8x repetition). 'bugs/reliability -34.5' comes from n=9 launches (47 resample-repeated items).
MISSING MAKER COMMENT (complaint1.py:175): critical_panel() defines maker_comment=None and cmd_run() never passes maker_comment on any launch.
decision: Do NOT treat critical-commenter selection as falsified; test person-built critical/reviewer comments standalone at size n without prepending 22 unchanged persona items, and replace the word-list regex with a sentiment/complaint classifier.

title: AUDIT CORRECTION: PRODUCT-USE-0 contaminated by pre-2025 tech giants, desktop-only apps, and NaN drop bias
question: Audit of PRODUCT-USE-0 code (pu0_build.py, pu0_score.py) and GCS pu0_score.json
scoring_fixed_before_results: PREREG 12 committed 02:05:51Z (037f02901); outputs.json written 05:37:47Z; pu0_score.json written 05:38:32Z
what_ran: 70 products run (ledger row 305 wrongly says 66 products), ONLY 26 products had >=1 clean session, 25 scored on complaints, 14 scored on likes.
deviations: LEDGER MISMATCH: Ledger row 305 says '66 products' in what_ran; 66 was the count of clean sessions (66/210), whereas products_run=70 and products_scored=26 (25 complaints, 14 likes).

SEVERE PRETRAINING CONTAMINATION (pu0_build.py:17): Filtering reviews >=2025 sorted by n_reviews_2025 selected pre-2025 global giants: cursor, figma, openai, claude, github, stripe, aws, Spotify, Gmail, Jira, Zoom, NVIDIA, xcode. Gemini 2.5 Flash homepage baseline recited memorized pretraining reviews (e.g. Figma 0.75, Claude 0.50, GitHub 0.44), NOT homepage inference.

UNREACHABLE DESKTOP PRODUCTS INCLUDED: 'xcode' (macOS IDE) and 'NVIDIA' were given to a headless Linux browser to 'use in 10 minutes without paying'; xcode still counted as 2 'clean' sessions on developer.apple.com.

SCORER NaN BIAS (pu0_score.py:35-47): 'if tl and pl:' and 'if tc and pc:' return NaN instead of 0.0 when clean sessions produce 0 likes or 0 complaints (e.g. Figma had 2 clean sessions, 0 likes -> dropped from like_recall n=14 instead of 0.0).
decision: Reverse DEC-B-074's conclusion that product-use loses to homepage reading on review truth; restrict review-truth calibration to products first launched after Gemini's knowledge cutoff and web-accessible without desktop installs.

title: AUDIT WARNING: PRODUCT-USE-1 (running) has 4 code bugs in runner.py and score.py contradicting its ledger design
question: Does PRODUCT-USE-1's code match its registered design before tonight's Nov 26 first frozen run?
design: Audit of origin/claude/person-model-v2:experiments/simlab/product_use/{runner,score,control_homepage}.py @ ff79f5c7c against ledger row PRODUCT-USE-1
scoring_fixed_before_results: FAILS code-vs-design check BEFORE first night
deviations: BUG 1 - REORDER VIOLATES DESIGN (score.py:24-26): Ledger says 'launches with no clean session keep their structural place' and D-PU1-ACCESS-EXCLUDED says access failures never affect predictions. In fact, reorder() imputes missing sim_score with the MEDIAN sim_score and sorts all 15 launches purely by -sim_score, promoting untested/blocked #14-#15 launches above clean-tested #1-#3 launches that score below median, and discarding structural score completely.

BUG 2 - COMPARISON REASONS DROPPED (runner.py:216, score.py:47): runner.py collects reasons (A_vs_B, A_vs_C) in DEBRIEF but omits 'reasons' from OUT['findings'] columns; score.py sim_cands() omits comparison reasons (contradicting its own docstring line 6), while homepage control includes comparisons (line 53).

BUG 3 - COMPETITOR ACCESS FAILURE PENALIZES LAUNCH BY 50% (runner.py:209): sim_score = would_use * (0.5 if pd.isna(pref_score) else pref_score). When both competitors fail access, pref_score is NaN -> 0.5x penalty, whereas beating 1 clean competitor gives 1.0x. Violates D-PU1-ACCESS-EXCLUDED.

BUG 4 - SKIPPED UNREACHABLE SITES VANISH & UNMERGED CANDIDATES SLICED (runner.py:67,209; score.py:52): SKIPPED ('platform_only') is never appended to rows/findings, so unreachable apps get no findings and get median sim_score in score.py; sim_cands() slices [:14] raw unmerged items in user order without LLM deduplication, dropping users 3-4.
BIAS 5 - POSITION & INCUMBENT BIAS (runner.py:163): Target launch is hardcoded as 'Product A' (never shuffled) and compared against 2 established category leaders rather than peer day-1 launches.
notes: Must fix before 09:27Z Nov 26 trigger runs.

title: AUDIT CORRECTION: CEILING-2 '1.20x human precision ceiling' is an item-packing artefact; launch-block hurt complaints to 0.57x
question: Audit of CEILING-1/CEILING-2 split-half human ceiling methodology and POINT-1 launch-block effect
scoring_fixed_before_results: No: CEILING-1 commit 88b9f8f8e (20:58Z), ceiling1.json written 21:07Z; CEILING-2 commit 4466f6f52 (21:11Z), ceiling2.json written 21:17Z; mixed ratio_of_means vs mean_of_ratios in report
what_ran: Re-derived from ceiling2.json: 22 launches (16 Nov 15-22 + 6 Nov 24-25), 8 resamples.
deviations: ITEM-PACKING ARTEFACT (ceiling1.py:171): Each single persona item concatenates 3 prompted fields ('{reaction} Concern: {concern} Question: {question}', ~250-300 dense chars), whereas 1 real PH comment in ceiling_half_a includes short 'Congrats on the launch!' comments. Matching item count n does NOT match information density, artificially inflating per-item precision (58.5% vs 50.8% ceiling = 1.20x).
ASYMMETRIC TRUNCATION (ceiling1.py:276,282): Half-B truth uses 500 chars/comment and ceil(U/2) users; Half-A ceiling uses 300 chars/comment and floor(U/2) users.
STATISTIC CHERRY-PICKING: Plan/log report mean-of-ratios for recall (0.92x) and precision (1.20x) where higher, but switch to ratio-of-means for complaint_recall (0.77x vs 0.91x mean-of-ratios).

UNREPORTED REGRESSION FROM POINT-1 LAUNCH BLOCK: On the 6 Nov 24-25 launches with the deployed launch-page block, deployed_eq loses to persona_eq on recall (-7.2 pts), precision (+2.6 pts), and complaint recall (18.8% vs 21.5%, and 0.57x ratio-of-means vs ceiling).
decision: Normalize split-half human ceiling by substantive non-congrats comments or total token budget, and audit POINT-1 launch-page block for complaint suppression.

title: AUDIT CORRECTION: POINT-1 deployed launch-page block without a no-block control arm; Opus A3 failed on 52% of rows
question: Did POINT-1 test whether adding the launch-page block improves over not having it?
scoring_fixed_before_results: No design logged prior to results
what_ran: 296 rows; A0..A3 all included the launch-page block (incl. up to 900 chars of maker's first comment); compared only against ref_other_commenter.
deviations: MISSING CONTROL ARM (run_point1.py:8-14): Every simulated arm (A0, A1, A2, A3) was given the new launch-page block. No arm ran Flash+history WITHOUT the block on the 296 rows (where ref_other_commenter shifted from 20.0% in CONTENT-LABELS-1 to 15.9% here). Deploying the block in DEC-B-073 had zero paired A/B evidence for the block itself.
MASSIVE SILENT DROP ON OPUS A3: Opus 5.5 returned empty output on 155 of 296 rows (52.4% failure rate), so +7.1% was scored on a non-random 141-row subset, not noted in RESEARCH_LOG.md line 2849.
decision: Evaluate E5's forward shadow (person_built_panel vs person_built_panel_noblock) paired on both same-point and complaint recall before keeping the maker-comment block.

title: AUDIT CORRECTION: RESID-BACKTEST-1 GCS outputs predate its 'assignment' log timestamp by 35 minutes
question: Was RESID-BACKTEST-1 registered/designed before running?
design: Timestamp check (AUDIT_GUIDE step 2): RESEARCH_LOG.md line 2868 vs gsutil ls -l gs://.../tmp/resid_backtest1/days/
what_ran: 60 backtest days written to GCS from 2026-11-25T06:40:33Z (2026-04-15.json) to 08:02:55Z (2026-10-31.json).
deviations: TIMESTAMP AUDIT FAILURE: Ledger row 309 and RESEARCH_LOG.md:2868 state RESID-BACKTEST-1 was assigned at 2026-11-25T07:15Z, but 26 day output files in GCS were written between 06:40:33Z and 07:14:14Z (35 minutes earlier). RESEARCH_LOG.md lines 2864-2905 contain multiple hand-estimated out-of-order timestamps (e.g. 07:15Z before 06:35Z; 19:00Z before 14:35Z; 21:00Z before 17:35Z), violating the Nov 2 UTC-clock rule.
DESIGN MISMATCH: Design required launch-page block, but run_resid_backtest.py:20-21 ran no-block shadow and VADER sentiment only.
COST MISMATCH: Measured cost in score.json is $17.80 vs $18.40 in RESEARCH_LOG.md and SOCIAL_SIM_PLAN.md.
decision: Enforce programmatic UTC timestamps and pre-run git commit checks in simharness/ledger.py before any API spend.

title: AUDIT CORRECTION: STRUCT-BT26 pred_votes calibrated on all-time post-launch warehouse votes and checked on 282 (not 328) days
question: Audit of STRUCT-BT26 code (struct_bt_write.py) and backtest_v2.json
scoring_fixed_before_results: registered retroactively after run (14:40Z output vs 21:30Z ledger commit)
what_ran: 328 day files written, but pred_votes_check only evaluated 282 days.
deviations: UNREPORTED SAMPLE DROP: Ledger row 4 reports days=328 next to pred_votes_day_ratio_median=1.004, omitting that pred_votes_check in backtest_v2.json covered only 282 days (46 days with <10 non-null warehouse vote rows excluded).

POST-CLOSE VOTE DRIFT: struct_bt_write.py:32 maps W.votes from the cumulative warehouse table updated months later rather than end-of-day launch votes, inflating predicted vote scale for older launches relative to 24h close.
decision: Calibrate pred_votes against 24h day-close vote snapshots where available rather than multi-month cumulative warehouse totals.
